| Q3 2024 | 65.2 | — | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q4 2024 | 100.3 | +53.8% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q1 2025 | 99.9 | −0.4% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q2 2025 | 103.0 | +3.1% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q3 2025 | 118.6 | +15.1% | 70.6 | 43.9 | 28.0% |
| Q4 2025 | 134.3 | +13.2% | 54.0 | 74.9 | ~30%* |

*Q4 2025 GAAP gross margin implied from the FY2025 full-year figure of 30.0% reported in the [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm). Q4 2025 marked the first quarter in which datacenter revenue exceeded CATV — a mix shift management cited as structurally significant entering FY2026. *n/d* = not separately disclosed in the relevant filing for that period.

---

## C. Primary Source Registry

**SEC Filings**

- [FY2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm) — Filed March 2026 for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2025. Source for Q3 2025 segment revenue detail (CATV $70.6M, datacenter $43.9M), GAAP gross margin of 28.0%, non-GAAP gross margin of 31.0%, and nine-month year-to-date financial statements.

leadership.key_finding: AAOI is structurally Thompson Lin's company. He founded it in 1997, has been Chairman/President/CEO since inception, and after 28+ years remains the dominant executive presence. The board around him includes a substantive laser/optics-industry veteran (Richard Black, ex-CEO ECRM the laser-imaging company sold to Kodak in 2021) and an Asia-semi industry insider (Che-Wei Lin, President of ASMedia and Corporate VP at ASUSTek). The composition reflects AAOI's actual operating profile — Sugar Land vertical integration plus Taiwan-China-US manufacturing — rather than the financial-engineering board that a near-IPO or pre-listing company would assemble. There is no separate COO. CFO Stefan Murry also serves as Chief Strategy Officer (dual role).

leadership.board_composition_observation: The board is unusually substantive for a sub-$1B small-cap that operates in optical/photonics. Three directors — Black (laser imaging), Che-Wei Lin (Asia semi/chipsets), DeLaney (Shell trading/EE) — carry deep technical and operating experience in adjacent industries; Loboa brings academic rigor; Yeh brings community-banking and real-estate stability; Chen brings cross-border industrial experience. There is no separate financial-engineering board member of the kind Sivers assembled (no ex-Citi CFO, no ex-Deutsche Bank Head of Corporate Finance) — AAOI's board is built for OPERATIONAL governance of a vertically-integrated semi company, not for a pending US listing or transformative M&A. That difference matters. AAOI is run by a founder-CEO who is also chairman. The board is configured to advise and audit, not to drive strategic change.

counterparties.key_finding: AAOI's counterparty map is the most concentrated for any small-cap optical components manufacturer at this scale: two customers — Digicomm (CATV channel) and Microsoft (hyperscale datacenter) — represented 81.9% of FY2025 revenue. The Amazon warrant disclosed in March 2025 (up to 7.945M shares) makes AMZN a 'pending' third major customer, with the >$324M order book announced March-April 2026 likely flowing through that relationship. The customer base inverts conventional risk framing: extreme concentration is the symptom of being early in the AI-optics supply cycle when very few suppliers can ship qualified product, not a sign of distribution weakness. The supply side — laser-diode-grade epitaxial wafers, OSFP cage and connector vendors, optical-coupling micro-optics — is undisclosed but inferred to lean Taiwan/China-domestic given the vertical-integration posture.

customers_fy2025.name: Digicomm International
customers_fy2025.framing: Digicomm is a privately-held US distributor of broadband network equipment (acquired by The Beekman Group in 2018). Through this channel AAOI's HFC amplifier and Quantum18 / QuantumLink products reach Comcast, Charter, Cox, and other Tier-1 MSOs. The share tripled in two years on the back of the DOCSIS 4.0 / 1.8 GHz amplifier upgrade cycle driven by the cable industry's response to fiber competition.

customers_fy2025.name: Microsoft
customers_fy2025.products: Optical transceivers (400G historical, 800G OSFP DR8 ramping)
customers_fy2025.framing: Microsoft has been AAOI's anchor datacenter customer for several years. Share declined relatively in 2025 because total revenue grew 83%; absolute dollar value rose modestly. Microsoft's qualified position in the 800G ramp is the operational reason AAOI passed the 30% gross-margin threshold.

customers_fy2025.name: Amazon (AWS)
customers_fy2025.framing: The March 2025 stock purchase warrant — up to 7.945M shares of AAOI common stock tied to purchase volume thresholds — formalises Amazon as a strategic hyperscale customer. The order announcements of March-April 2026 ($53M + $71M + $200M+ = >$324M) are widely understood by analysts to be Amazon, though AOI's press releases describe only 'one major hyperscale customer.' AAOI's 10-K does not yet name Amazon as a >10% customer — the recognition lag reflects the warrant-vesting and purchase-cycle timing rather than relationship absence.

supply_chain_observations.vertical_integration: AAOI fabricates its own InP and GaAs laser dies using MBE (molecular beam epitaxy) and MOCVD processes in-house. This eliminates the largest upstream dependency that pure-play module-assemblers (Eoptolink, Innolight, Sumitomo OEM lines) carry: the InP wafer supply chain dominated by Sumitomo Electric, II-VI/Coherent and a handful of Asian foundries.
remaining_external_dependencies: OSFP / QSFP-DD cage and connector vendors (TE Connectivity, Amphenol, Molex)
Optical lens and isolator suppliers (predominantly Japanese — Nichia, Hamamatsu indirect)
DSPs and clock-data-recovery silicon for the higher-line-rate transceivers (Marvell, Maxlinear, Broadcom)
Capacitors, resistors, PCB substrates (commoditised — Taiwan/China sourcing)
supply_chain_observations.geographic_concentration: Manufacturing concentrated in three locations: Sugar Land (Texas), Taipei (Taiwan), Ningbo (China). The Ningbo facility represents the largest single point of employee concentration (2,881 of 4,691 employees, 61.4%). The Texas-onshore 800G capability (35% of exit-2025 800G capacity) is the strategic hedge against China-US trade friction and the basis for the 'largest US production capacity' marketing claim.
